title: Getting started with Claude.ai
author: Anthropic
summary: A guided tour of the Claude chat window: writing a first prompt, attaching documents, turning on search and research mode, choosing a model, switching writing styles, and using extended thinking.
who_for: Someone opening Claude for the first time who wants one clear pass over every control before starting real work.
skip_if: Skip if you already use Claude most days, because this never goes past explaining what each button does.

title: Getting started with projects in Claude.ai
author: Anthropic
summary: Shows how to build a Project so Claude keeps the same context across many chats: creating it, loading a knowledge base, writing project instructions, and sharing it with a team.
who_for: People who repeat the same kind of task and keep pasting the same background material into every new conversation.
skip_if: Skip if you only ask Claude one-off questions, because Projects add setup work you will not get back.

title: Getting started with research in Claude.ai
author: Anthropic
summary: Demonstrates Claude's Research mode on multi-source questions: how to word the request, how it works together with extended thinking, and where it replaces hours of manual searching.
who_for: Anyone who does market scans, competitor checks, or background reading by hand and wants Claude to do the first pass.
skip_if: Skip if you need controlled academic sourcing, because this is a short feature demo and says nothing about citation quality.

title: What are skills?
author: Anthropic
summary: A short explainer of Agent Skills: you teach Claude a procedure one time, and Claude then applies it automatically whenever the situation matches.
who_for: Anyone who keeps hearing the word Skills and wants the idea clearly in under three minutes before opening the docs.
skip_if: Skip if you want to build a Skill today, because this explains only the concept and shows no file structure or authoring steps.

title: Getting started with Claude Cowork
author: Anthropic
summary: Walks through Cowork, where Claude works on the real files on your computer. You describe the job in plain words and Claude finds the documents and edits them itself.
who_for: Non-developers whose work sits in folders of documents and spreadsheets instead of in a chat window.
skip_if: Skip if your plan does not include Cowork, because you cannot follow along with any of it.

title: Getting started with Claude in Excel
author: Anthropic
summary: Shows Claude reading a whole workbook, including nested formulas and linked tabs, then explaining results with cell-level citations and changing assumptions without breaking the formulas.
who_for: Analysts and finance people who live in spreadsheets and want Claude to audit or extend a model they did not write.
skip_if: Skip if you are on the free plan, because Claude in Excel is a research preview for Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise only.

title: Lesson 1: Introduction to AI Fluency | AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations Course |
author: Anthropic
summary: Opens Anthropic's free AI Fluency course, made with Prof. Rick Dakan and Prof. Joseph Feller, by arguing that the skill worth learning is collaboration with AI, not the technology behind it.
who_for: People starting the AI Fluency course, and teachers deciding whether to set it for a class.
skip_if: Skip if you want hands-on Claude technique, because this lesson only sets up the course frame and teaches no prompting.

title: Lesson 2B: The 4D Framework | AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations Course
author: Anthropic
summary: Introduces the four core competencies at the centre of the course, called the 4Ds: Delegation, Description, Discernment and Diligence.
who_for: Anyone who wants shared words for judging their own AI use instead of guessing whether a result was good.
skip_if: Skip if you dislike frameworks and learn better from worked examples, because this lesson is all structure.

title: Lesson 7: Effective prompting techniques (Deep Dive) | AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations Course
author: Anthropic
summary: The most practical lesson in the AI Fluency course: concrete ways to phrase, structure and refine prompts when you work with an assistant like Claude.
who_for: Non-developers who want real prompting technique without any API or code talk.
skip_if: Skip if you build on the API, because Anthropic's own prompt engineering deep dive covers far more for that audience.

title: AI prompt engineering: A deep dive
author: Anthropic
summary: Four Anthropic prompt engineering practitioners talk through how they really write prompts, where beginners go wrong, and how prompting changes as models get stronger. Unscripted roundtable with chapter markers.
who_for: People past basic prompting who want judgment and reasoning rather than another list of tips.
skip_if: Skip if you have never prompted Claude yourself, because the whole discussion assumes you have already hit these problems.
notes: 591,531 views, 1:16:42, channel @anthropic-ai, verified 2026-08-22. Published 2024, so some model-specific detail is now dated; the reasoning still holds.

title: Prompting 101 | Code w/ Claude
author: Anthropic
summary: Hannah Moran and Christian Ryan from Anthropic's Applied AI team build one real prompt on stage from nothing, adding structure, examples and constraints step by step and showing what each change fixes.
who_for: Developers writing their first production prompts who want to watch the whole edit loop, not just the finished prompt.
skip_if: Skip if you only use the Claude chat app, because the session is framed around API calls and system prompts.
notes: 484,385 views, 24:52, channel @anthropic-ai, recorded at Code w/ Claude San Francisco, verified 2026-08-22

title: What is Claude Code?
author: Anthropic
summary: Explains what Claude Code is, an agent in your terminal that reads the codebase, edits files and runs commands, and how that differs from chatting on Claude.ai.
who_for: Developers about to install Claude Code who want the mental model before the first command.
skip_if: Skip if you have already run Claude Code on a real task, because nothing here will be new.
notes: 7,740,673 views, 2:55, channel @claude, lesson 1 of the free Claude Code course at claude.com/courses, verified 2026-08-22

title: The CLAUDE.md file
author: Anthropic
summary: Covers what belongs in a CLAUDE.md file, how the hierarchy resolves across user, project and directory levels, and how to keep the file from turning into noise.
who_for: Developers whose Claude Code sessions keep forgetting the project's conventions.
skip_if: Skip if you already maintain a tuned CLAUDE.md, because this stays at the level of writing your first one.
notes: 500,360 views, 3:01, channel @claude, part of the free Claude Code course, verified 2026-08-22

title: The Explore → Plan → Code → Commit workflow in Claude Code
author: Anthropic
summary: The workflow Anthropic pushes hardest: make Claude research the code and plan before it writes, state what success looks like, then have a subagent review the work before you push.
who_for: Developers whose Claude Code output arrives fast but wrong, and who need a discipline that fixes it.
skip_if: Skip if you already plan and review before you commit, because this only names a habit you have.
notes: 434,078 views, 3:11, channel @claude, part of the free Claude Code course, verified 2026-08-22

title: MCP in Claude Code
author: Anthropic
summary: How to attach MCP servers such as Linear, GitHub and documentation sources to Claude Code, scope them for a project or a team, and keep the context cost under control.
who_for: Developers ready to connect Claude Code to the tools their team already uses every day.
skip_if: Skip if you have not used Claude Code yet, because MCP only pays off once your basic loop works.
notes: 299,741 views, 3:37, channel @claude, part of the free Claude Code course, verified 2026-08-22

title: Mastering Claude Code in 30 minutes
author: Anthropic
summary: One sitting that runs through Claude Code's advanced features, keyboard shortcuts and working patterns, recorded for the Code w/ Claude developer conference.
who_for: Developers who have Claude Code installed and know they are using a small part of it.
skip_if: Skip if you have never opened Claude Code, because the pace assumes you already know the basic loop.
notes: 1,554,875 views, 28:07, channel @anthropic-ai, verified 2026-08-22. Recorded May 2025, so the interface has moved on in places.

title: Claude Code best practices | Code w/ Claude
author: Anthropic
summary: Cal Rueb of Anthropic's technical staff shows the working habits the team uses internally: how to scope a task, when to reset context, and where Claude Code breaks down if you let it run loose.
who_for: Developers already shipping with Claude Code who want the internal playbook rather than the marketing version.
skip_if: Skip if you have not written a CLAUDE.md yet, because the advice assumes the basics are already in place.
notes: 545,896 views, 25:53, channel @anthropic-ai, recorded at Code w/ Claude San Francisco, verified 2026-08-22

title: Beyond the basics with Claude Code
author: Anthropic
summary: The 2026 follow-on to the beginner course: writing a CLAUDE.md that earns its place, wiring tools in through MCP, packaging team knowledge as Skills, and running auto mode safely.
who_for: Teams standardising how everyone uses Claude Code, not only individual developers.
skip_if: Skip if you are still learning the basic prompt loop, because this assumes you already ship with Claude Code daily.

title: The Model Context Protocol (MCP)
author: Anthropic
summary: Theo Chu, David Soria Parra and Alex Albert explain what MCP is, its core components, why Anthropic open-sourced it, and how it changed the way applications connect Claude to outside data and tools.
who_for: Developers and technical product managers deciding whether to build on MCP at all.
skip_if: Skip if you want to write an MCP server today, because this stays conceptual and shows no code.
notes: 246,648 views, 19:35, channel @anthropic-ai, chapter markers in description, verified 2026-08-22

title: Tips for building AI agents
author: Anthropic
summary: Barry Zhang, Erik and Alex Albert of Anthropic separate agents from plain workflows, break down the anatomy of an agent prompt, and name the failure patterns they keep seeing in real builds.
who_for: Engineers designing their first agent who want to skip the mistakes everyone makes.
skip_if: Skip if a single well-shaped prompt already solves your problem, because agents add cost and failure modes you do not need.
